Lower-probability tails above 33°C remain possible only with localized heat buildup or forecast revisions from updated model runs.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current forecasts for Shanghai on August 20, 2026, point to a daily maximum near 31–33 °C under typical late-summer monsoon conditions.** Short-range models from sources such as timeanddate and regional meteorological services show highs around 32–33 °C (roughly 90–91 °F) with scattered thundershowers and high humidity, which tend to cap daytime peaks while preventing rapid radiative cooling.

The market’s heavy weighting on 31 °C (42.5 %) and 32 °C (26.5 %) reflects this consensus: ongoing cloudy-to-overcast skies and convective activity observed in recent days (Aug 16–18) have kept observed highs in the low-to-mid 30s, and similar steering patterns are expected to persist. A modest 30 °C outcome (18.5 %) remains plausible if stronger or earlier rainfall suppresses insolation.

Higher probabilities for 33 °C or above are limited by the absence of a strong high-pressure ridge or clear-sky setup that would allow temperatures to climb further, while sub-30 °C outcomes are discounted because climatological baselines for mid-August already sit near 31 °C. Updated model runs and official Shanghai Meteorological Observatory briefings over the next 24–48 hours will be the key catalysts for any shift in these implied probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) activity across Luzon, including Metro Manila, is the dominant driver behind trader positioning for Manila’s August 20 high temperature. Official PAGASA guidance through mid-August shows cloudy skies, scattered showers, and thunderstorms expected to continue, limiting solar insolation and promoting evaporative cooling that caps daytime maxima near seasonal norms of 30–32 °C. The tight clustering around 31 °C (37.5 %) and 32 °C (32 %) reflects model consensus on sustained cloud cover and rainfall timing, while the modest 33 °C probability (14.5 %) accounts for possible brief clearing or delayed convection. Conversely, heavier or earlier monsoon bursts could suppress readings toward 30 °C or lower. With resolution only two days away, the next PAGASA update and short-range model runs will be the key catalysts for any shift in implied probabilities.
